reviews.review_msg: Engaging lectures, but can be dry at times. Attendance is mandatory, but not too difficult if you use resources like Unstuck ai for study prep. Exams are fair, just require consistent effort.
Lectures are alright, she gives alot of resources so youll be well prepared for exams. In class quizzes are definitely kind of annoying though
painful lecture, why cant school just find someone who can actually explain things in English

She is not a good prof. You don't know if you will have a normal lecture or get ripped into cause she isn't in a good mood and not understanding in her way. In-class quizzes worth 15% of your mark randomly sprinkled around and horrible examples. If I have the chance to choose between her and Craig (another prof) I choose Craig Scratchly.
"No more than 1 unmarketable tomtato" ahh prof
Kinda dry lectures, but is tolerable. Fairly easy exams. You have to be trying REALLY hard to actually fail this class.
Snooze fest

top 1 worst professor on planet earth. i would rather roll on the floor for 2 hours compared to sitting in this lecture i would learn more

honestly though, she spends more time calling students out for not actively participating in class. according to her, if you arent actively answering questions, you should leave the class
Her lecture notes are confusing and courses are designed only to fulfill the 4-credit requirement.
I found her lectures and explanation of key concepts very helpful and easy to follow.

Lectures are poorly structured with no evident links between overarching ideas. 90% of the class consists of examples, which are tediously done to minute detail. This wastes an incredible amount of time, and doesn't help understanding.  Talks very slowly. I watched her online lectures at 2x the speed and found it to be akin to normal speech.

So this professor, instead of using the standard lon-capa or what not, making her students pay $90 to look at the assignment questions on a website that won't even load on Chrome half the time. A professor that thrives on ripping students off is not a professor to be respected. Oh, do I even mention her wasting time on those stupid "experiments"?
A funny prof who does lots of interesting survey. His notes and lectures are very helpful. Exams are ok as long as you do his assignments and labs. And yes, watch out for his pop quiz.
Well prepared before class, very enthusiastic, and helpful.  Course is easy if you use his notes and do the assigned homework.  Watch out for pop quizzes.
280 was OKAY. Wait till you take ENSC225 with him :)

This guy stinks at teaching. He's incredibly boring, and it's obvious to see that he has 0 interest in what he teaches. The previous offering for 280 exposed you to R and a Matlab project. Nothing like that was to be seen this time around. Instead, we had the pleasure of calculating standard deviations for 30 data values for our exams...

Lectures are a copy paste of the textbook. All assignments and exams are pulled from textbook problems. I didn't find the content very engaging during lectures but he tries his best to involve students. Overall just a very average prof, nothing super great or bad to say. The class material is pretty easy if you take the time to do assignments.

Not great, lectures are copy-pasted from the textbook. Lectures are a waste of your time, just read the textbook on your own. Formulas are not always given. The class is annoying but not necessarily hard, but prepare to do most of the learning on your own.

Professor majid is one of the best and most caring profs I have encountered at SFU, coming into classes he would make everyone feel welcomed with new slides for each lecture and always had an upbeat mood cracking jokes... has an odd fascination with fishes. His exams were easy and fair and always had enough material to review with textbook guides.

Major's monotone voice and direct textbook copied slides make his lectures a drag to sit through. Use the textbook instead of lecture slides for future since he is prone to adding spelling errors in anything from a minor word that wouldn't impact understanding to a blatantly false formula every now and then.

A great choice for an introductory statistics class. Clear easy to follow lectures and homework assigned from textbooks. Uploads notes after lectures. Tests are homework questions with different numbers so studying homework is good test preparation. The labs and term projects are shallow, token, and useless; but the program requires them.
